answer: Time-locked task grove. Each identity must solve a fresh, randomly generated physical simulation task whose parameters are drawn from a sealed hardware source; answers are verified against a copper-standard reference run, and the inlet for new identities opens only when the prior task's unused solutions expire. Submitting a copied or precomputed answer fails because the task seed is unrepeatable. An attacker must provision real compute for every identity, paying the full simulation cost per attempt with no reuse across accounts.
